newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa, DAG union due to meet on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa, DAG union due to meet on Friday.

text.p: Top officials of Lufthansa AG and the DAG union will use a meeting on Friday in Hamburg as a forum to discuss the growing wage conflict between the airline and the union, industry sources said on Wednesday.
The meeting was originally scheduled to discuss the German airline's restructuring plans, the sources said.
A DAG spokesman confirmed the meeting had been scheduled to take place and that the wage dispute was not a topic on the agenda.
A Lufthansa spokesman declined comment on the meeting.
But industry sources said the wage dispute would be discussed after the DAG said on Wednesday pilots had voted in favour of a strike-authorisation ballot should wage talks fail.
Flight attendants and ground personnel at the airline had failed to reach the minimum quorum needed for their participation in any strike, the union said.
"I think it would be fair to assume that the wage dispute will come up as a topic of discussion after the DAG released the strike ballot results," the source told Reuters.
Lufthansa had originally scheduled the meeting to discuss the announced plans to restructure its passenger services areas into one division.
But the airline has so far failed to reach a wage deal with pilots, flight attendants and ground personnel who are represented by the DAG, amid a growing threat of a strike.

Union members, upset with Lufthansa seeking to lock them into a 27-month deal at a time of industry turbulence, staged last November and December two warning strikes that interrupted flights and cost the airline about 30 million marks ($18 million).

Lufthansa has said it would not change its standing offer to the union, which includes a one-off payment equal to one-third of a month's base pay, a 1.8 percent pay hike and 500 marks of participation in Lufthansa's 1996 profit.
